'''Jaime Jaquez Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|'|h|aɪ|m|ɛ|_|'|h|ɑː|k|ɛ|z}} {{respell|HY|meh|_|HAH|kez}};<ref>{{cite web |date=November 10, 2023 |title=Inside the HEAT: Jaime Jaquez Jr. |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OhdxmUPcHJ8&t=280s |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=Luis Claudio De Jesús Charles |language=en |format=video |time=280 seconds}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=November 10, 2023 |title=Inside the HEAT: Jaime Jaquez Jr. |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OhdxmUPcHJ8&t=736s |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=Luis Claudio De Jesús Charles |language=en |format=video |time=736 seconds}}</ref> born February 18, 2001) is a Mexican-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. During his [[Senior (education)|senior]] season in 2023, he was recognized as a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]]. Over the course of his collegiate career, Jaquez was selected three times to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] team, including two first-team honors, and was twice named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team. He was selected by the Miami Heat with the 18th overall pick in the first round of the [[2023 NBA draft]]. Jaquez is also known by the nickname "'''Juan Wick'''," which reflects his [[Mexicans|Mexican]] heritage and a perceived resemblance to the character [[John Wick (character)|John Wick]].<ref name="chazaro_12072023">{{cite news |last=Chazaro |first=Alan |date=December 7, 2023 |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. on Becoming the Breakout Rookie of This NBA Season |url=https://www.gq.com/story/jaime-jaquez-jr-interview |access-date=January 2, 2024 |work=[[GQ|GQ Sports]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Jeff |date=November 30, 2023 |title=Heat Rookie Jaime Jaquez Jr. Embraces New Nickname With Open Arms |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/11/30/miami-heat-jaime-jaquez-jr-nickname-juan-wick |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref>

==Early life==
Jaquez was born on February 18, 2001, in [[Irvine, California]],<ref>{{cite basketball-reference|name=Jaime Jaquez Jr.|id=j/jaqueja01|access-date=October 18, 2025}}</ref> and grew up in [[Camarillo, California|Camarillo]].<ref name=usab/> He is the third generation in his family to play [[college basketball]]. His parents, Angela ([[Birth name#Maiden and married names|née]] Sather) and Jaime Sr., both played basketball at [[Concordia University Irvine]], where they first met.<ref name="bolch">{{cite news |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=November 28, 2019 |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. giving Mick Cronin what he wants for UCLA's rebuild |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2019-11-28/jaime-jaquez-jr-giving-mick-cronin-what-he-wants-for-ucla-rebuild |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Rosehart |first=Ben |date=November 1, 2022 |title=CUI Excited For Rare Opportunity to Play At UCLA |url=https://cuigoldeneagles.com/news/2022/11/1/mens-basketball-cui-excited-for-rare-opportunity-to-play-at-ucla.aspx |access-date=November 9, 2023 |website=CUI Golden eagles}}</ref> His paternal grandfather, Ezequiel, immigrated to [[California]] from [[Mexico]] as a child and played basketball at [[Ventura College]] and [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona University]].<ref name="Legacy">{{cite web |last=Medcalf |first=Myron |date=March 3, 2023 |title=The third-generation basketball legacy of UCLA's Gabriela and Jaime Jaquez Jr. |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35755017 |access-date=March 3, 2023 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kivowitz |first=Elizabeth |last2=Ramos |first2=Barbra |date=April 17, 2023 |title=New scholarship fund for UCLA students named for sporting Jaquez family |url=https://newsroom.ucla.edu/releases/scholarship-fund-for-latino-students-named-for-jaquez-family |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA Newsroom]]}}</ref>

==High school career==
Jaquez attended [[Adolfo Camarillo High School]] in [[Camarillo, California]], and graduated in 2019. As a [[freshman]], he averaged 15.3 points, 10.0 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 2.3 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 2.6 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game, leading the team to a 25–7 record and an appearance in the [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) semifinals. In his [[sophomore]] season, he earned All-[[Ventura County, California|Ventura County]] second-team honors while averaging 24.1 points, 10.9 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and 2.6 steals per game, despite missing 12 games due to an [[Sprained ankle|ankle injury]].<ref name=usab>{{cite web |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/j/jaquez-jr-jaime.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220422234315/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/j/jaquez-jr-jaime.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 22, 2022 |website=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=April 2, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 12, 2017 |title=Camarillo's Jaquez Jr. out indefinitely |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2017/01/12/camarillos-jaquez-jr-out-indefinitely/96518436/ |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Ventura County Star]]}}</ref> During his [[senior (education)|senior]] season, Jaquez averaged 31.7 points, 11.7 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.1 steals per game, guiding the team to a 25–4 record and its first [[Coastal Canyon League]] (CCL) title.<ref name="ledin">{{cite news |last=Ledin |first=Loren |title=Camarillo's Jaime Jaquez Jr. is The Star's Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2019/03/16/camarillos-jaquez-jr-stars-boys-basketball-player-year/3098491002/ |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[Ventura County Star]] |date=March 16, 2019}}</ref> He received first-team All-[[CIF Southern Section]] honors and finished his high school career with a total of 2,653 points.<ref name="tay">{{cite news |last=Tay |first=Jared |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. hopes to make familia proud, aims to inspire future Latino players |url=https://dailybruin.com/2020/02/28/jaime-jaquez-jr-hopes-to-make-familia-proud-aims-to-inspire-future-latino-players/ |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=The Daily Bruin |date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> Jaquez also set a school single-game scoring record with a 54-point performance against [[Royal High School (California)|Royal High School]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gomez |first=Eric |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. eyes hoop dreams at UCLA, Mexico, PanAms |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/27287297 |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 31, 2019}}</ref> In addition to basketball, he also played as a [[pitcher]] on the school's [[baseball]] team.<ref name="ledin" />

==College career==
[[File:Jaime Jaquez Jr.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Jaquez as a [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] [[freshman]] in 2019]]
Jaquez was [[college recruiting|recruited]] to the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), by then-[[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]]' coach [[Steve Alford]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Seth|last=Gleeson|title='Making two countries proud' UCLA's Jaime Jáquez Jr. playing for both Mexican and American heritages|date=April 2, 2021|work=USA Today|url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/04/02/final-four-ucla-jaime-jaquez-jr-playing-mexican-american-heritages/4840492001/|access-date=June 27, 2023}}</ref> who offered him a [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]] at the end of his [[junior (education year)|junior]] year. However, Alford was fired in 2018, replaced later by [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]], who had recruited Jaquez while coaching at [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]]. Jaquez did not seriously pursue another school, and remained [[National Letter of Intent|committed]] to UCLA.<ref name=davis_09302022>{{cite web|first=Seth|last=Davis|title=UCLA's Jaime Jaquez Jr. understands what it takes to win: 'Half the battle is wanting it more'|date=September 30, 2022|work=The Athletic|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3641983/2022/09/30/ucla-jaime-jaquez-basketball/|url-access=subscription|access-date=June 27, 2023}}</ref> He became a [[starting lineup|starter]] for the Bruins during the [[2019 Maui Invitational|2019 Maui Jim Maui Invitational]],<ref name="tay"/> after recording 17 points and 12 rebounds in a 74–48 win against [[Chaminade Silverswords|Chaminade]] on November 26.<ref name=bolch/> On December 1, he scored a season-high 18 points in a 93–64 win over [[2019–20 San Jose State Spartans men's basketball team|San Jose State]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Jaquez, Hill lead UCLA to 93–64 win over San Jose State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170605 |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 1, 2019}}</ref> On February 27, 2020, he scored 18 points and shot the game-winning three-pointer with 0.6 seconds remaining in a 75–72 win over [[2019–20 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Vanoni |first=Maggie |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s shot lifts UCLA men's basketball into first-place tie in Pac-12 |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2020/02/27/jaime-jaquez-jr-s-shot-lifts-ucla-mens-basketball-into-first-place-tie-in-pac-12/ |accessdate=April 2, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |date=February 27, 2020}}</ref> Jaquez concluded his freshman [[2019–20 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|season]] averaging 8.9 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. His performance earned him an [[2019–20 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season#All-Freshman Team|honorable mention]] to the [[2019–20 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team.<ref>{{cite news |date=March 11, 2020 |title=Factoids on UCLA Hoops Heading into Pac-12 Tourney |url=https://247sports.com/college/ucla/Article/UCLA-Bruins-Basketball-UCLA-Basketball-News-and-Notes-144831374/ |accessdate=March 30, 2020 |work=[[247Sports]]}}</ref>

On February 18, 2021, Jaquez scored 25 points on his 20th birthday in a 74–60 win over [[2020–21 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]], the Bruins' fifth straight in its [[Arizona–UCLA men's basketball rivalry|rivalry with the Wildcats]].<ref>{{cite news|title=UCLA beats Arizona 74-60 to complete sweep of Wildcats|date=February 18, 2021|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401265426|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref> For the [[2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|season]], he was a second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] selection and was named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite news|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA PG Tyger Campbell earns Pac-12 first-team honors|date=March 9, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2021/03/09/ucla-pg-tyger-campbell-earns-pac-12-first-team-honors/|access-date=March 10, 2021}}</ref> In UCLA's First Four play-in game of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]], he led the Bruins in scoring with 27 points in a 86–80 overtime win against [[2020–21 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]].<ref>"[https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-03-18/ucla-michigan-state-first-four-ncaa-tournament UCLA Surges Late to Save Season and Defeat Michigan State in First Four Thriller]" ''Los Angeles Times. March 18, 2021.'' Retrieved March 18, 2021.</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=UCLA beats Michigan St 86-80 in overtime in First Four game|date=March 19, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/gametracker/recap/NCAAB_20210318_UCLA@MICHST/|access-date=March 19, 2021}}</ref> UCLA advanced to the [[Final four|Final Four]], ultimately losing 93–90 to [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] on April 3.<ref name=bolch_04062023>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. declares for the NBA draft, will forgo year of eligibility|date=April 6, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-04-06/ucla-star-jaime-jaquez-jr-declares-nba-draft|access-date=May 8, 2023}}</ref>

[[File:Caleb Daniels Jaime Jaquez Jr (cropped).jpg|thumb|Jaquez defending [[Caleb Daniels]] of [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] in 2021]]
Jaquez was restricted by ankle injuries throughout most of the [[2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2021–22 season]].<ref name="bolch_02282022" /><ref name="fattal_03222022">{{cite news|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s injury has UCLA preparing two game plans for UNC|date=March 22, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/03/22/jaime-jaquez-jr-s-injury-has-ucla-preparing-two-game-plans-for-unc/|access-date=March 23, 2022}}</ref> He suffered from [[synovitis]] in one ankle and began wearing [[ankle brace|braces]] on both ankles as a preventative measure.<ref name="bolch_03232022">{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=How Jaime Jaquez Jr. became the UCLA Bruins' toughest player|date=March 23, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-03-23/jaime-jaquez-jr-feature|access-date=March 24, 2022}}</ref> He bounced back from a three-game stretch in mid-February 2022 in which he scored a combined 13 points.<ref name="fattal_03222022" /> On February 28, Jaquez scored a career-high 30 points in a 77–66 win over [[2021–22 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]].<ref name=bolch_02282022>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s career-high 30 points power No. 17 UCLA past Washington|date=February 28, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-02-28/jaime-jaquez-jr-s-career-high-30-powers-no-17-ucla-over-washington|access-date=March 1, 2022}}</ref> In the following game, on March 5, he scored 27 points in the regular-season finale against [[2021–22 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]], helping UCLA end its five-game losing streak in their crosstown [[UCLA–USC rivalry|rivalry with the Trojans]].<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 17 UCLA beats No. 16 USC 75-68, finishes 2nd in Pac-12|date=March 5, 2022|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401377493|access-date=March 6, 2022}}</ref> He was named the Pac-12 Player of the Week after averaging 28.5 points on 64 percent shooting along with 7.5 rebounds, as the Bruins clinched the No. 2 seed in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pac-12 Men's Basketball Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva - March 7, 2022|date=March 7, 2022|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2022/3/7/pac-12-mens-basketball-performance-awards-presented-nextiva-march-7-2022.aspx|access-date=March 8, 2022}}</ref> Jaquez was named to the All-Pac-12 first team and was voted again to the conference's defensive team.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ryan|last=Kartje|title=UCLA's Johnny Juzang, USC's Isaiah Mobley among All-Pac-12 picks for Bruins, Trojans|date=March 8, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-03-08/all-pac-12-ucla-usc|access-date=March 8, 2022}}</ref> He was one of five finalists for the [[Julius Erving Award]], given to the top [[small forward]] in the country.<ref>{{cite news|first=Bill|last=Seals|title=Bruins take on the Trojans in a critical conference showdown|date=March 3, 2022|newspaper=Culver City Observer|url=https://www.culvercityobserver.com/story/2022/03/03/sports/bruins-take-on-the-trojans-in-a-critical-conference-showdown/11105.html|access-date=March 8, 2022}}</ref> In the second round of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]], on March 19, he scored 15 points in a 72–56 win over [[2021–22 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team|Saint Mary's]], but exited the game and did not return after [[Sprained ankle|spraining]] his right ankle with seven minutes remaining in the second half.<ref name=bolch_03232022/><ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA defeats St. Mary's to return to the Sweet 16 for the second straight year|date=March 19, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-19/ucla-defeats-saint-marys-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-sweet-16|access-date=March 19, 2022}}</ref> He was averaging 20.5 points in his last eight games, with the Bruins going 7–1.<ref name=thamel_03252022>{{cite news|first=Pete|last=Thamel |authorlink=Pete Thamel |title=UCLA's Jaime Jaquez Jr. hopeful for matchup vs. North Carolina despite sprained ankle|date=March 25, 2022|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33586261 |access-date=March 26, 2022}}</ref> The stretch coincided with him being able to resume practicing,<ref name=thamel_03252022/> while UCLA's leading scorer, [[Johnny Juzang]], was in a scoring slump.<ref name=bolch_03232022/> Jaquez recovered to play 38 minutes in the following game on March 25 against [[2021–22 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the Sweet Sixteen, but the Bruins lost 73–66. He scored 10 points, shooting 1-for-11 in the second half and missing his final nine shots.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA's March Madness run ends in heartbreaking Sweet 16 loss to North Carolina|date=March 25, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-25/ucla-mens-basketball-north-carolina-march-madness|access-date=March 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Eddie|last=Pells|title=If the shoe fits: Love leads Carolina over UCLA into Elite 8|date=March 25, 2022|publisher=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/march-madness-north-carolina-tar-heels-mens-basketball-st-peters-peacocks-mens-basketball-ucla-bruins-mens-basketball-sports-2a42c4860b70e73463551d9840189bc2|access-date=March 26, 2022}}</ref> Amid the injuries, Jaquez's 3-point shooting dropped to 27.6 percent. Along with needing [[surgery]] in April to remove [[Osteophyte|bone spurs]] from his right ankle, he decided against [[Eligibility for the NBA draft#"Early entry" player|declaring for the NBA draft]],<ref name=davis_09302022/> and returned to UCLA for his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. will return to UCLA in hopes of winning a national title|date=April 18, 2022|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-04-18/jaime-jaquez-announces-he-will-return-ucla-basketball|access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref>

For the second straight season, Jaquez was named a finalist for the Julius Erving Award in [[2022–23 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2022–23]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaquez Jr. Among Five Finalists for Julius Erving Award|date=March 8, 2023|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2023/3/8/mens-basketball-jaquez-jr-among-five-finalists-for-julius-erving-award.aspx|access-date=March 15, 2023}}</ref> On February 4, 2023, he had a game-high 24 points and a career-high 15 rebounds in a 76–52 win over [[2022–23 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=February 4, 2023 |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. powers No. 9 UCLA in a get-well rout of Washington State |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-02-04/ucla-beats-washington-state-jaime-jaquez-jr-recap |access-date=February 24, 2023 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> That month, he scored late baskets in multiple games to help lead the team to victories, including seven points in {{frac|3|1|2}} minutes as the Bruins secured a 78–71 win over [[2022–23 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]] on February 23.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=February 25, 2023 |title=Why UCLA's Jaime Jaquez Jr. is in race for Pac-12 player of year |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-02-24/ucla-basketball-jaime-jaquez-jr-in-player-of-year-race |access-date=February 26, 2023 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> He led UCLA to their first [[2022–23 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]] regular season title since [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013]].<ref name=fattal_03072023>{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA's Jaime Jaquez Jr. named Pac-12 Player of the Year|date=March 7, 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/07/uclas-jaime-jaquez-jr-named-pac-12-player-of-the-year/|access-date=March 8, 2023}}</ref> The Bruins received a No. 2 seed in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]]. In the opener, on March 16, Jaquez recorded 17 points, eight rebounds, and a career-high five steals in an 86–53 victory over No. 15-seed [[2022–23 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=March 16, 2023 |title=UCLA dodges upset trend, opens NCAA tournament with rout of UNC Asheville |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-16/ucla-vs-unc-asheville-ncaa-tournament-recap |access-date=March 18, 2023 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> Losing two starters, [[Adem Bona]] and [[Jaylen Clark]], due to injuries, UCLA concluded their season with a 79–76 loss to [[2022–23 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] in the Sweet Sixteen on March 23.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jubilation turns into heartbreak as UCLA loses to Gonzaga again in NCAA tournament|date=March 23, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-23/ucla-basketball-gonzaga-ncaa-tournament-sweet-16-recap|access-date=March 24, 2023}}</ref> For the season, Jaquez averaged 17.8 points and 8.2 rebounds.<ref name=bolch_04062023/> He was named a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]],<ref>{{cite press release|title=Pac-12 Men's Basketball Weekly Rundown - March 15, 2023|date=March 15, 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2023/3/15/pac-12-mens-basketball-weekly-rundown-march-15-2023.aspx|access-date=March 16, 2023}}</ref> and received the [[Lute Olson Award]] as the college player of the year.<ref name=bolch_04062023/> Jaquez was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]], becoming the first Bruin to win since [[Kevin Love]] in [[2007–08 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2008]] and the first UCLA senior to capture the award since [[Ed O'Bannon]] in [[1994–95 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1995]].<ref name=pac12_03072023>{{cite press release|title=2022-23 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|date=March 7, 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2023/3/7/2022-23-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance.aspx|access-date=March 7, 2023}}</ref> He also earned his second consecutive first-team all-conference selection.<ref name=fattal_03072023/> After the season, Jaquez declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], forgoing the extra year of [[National Collegiate Athletic Association#Player eligibility|eligibility]] that was available due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]]. He ended his career ranked eighth in UCLA history in career scoring (1,802) and career steals (178), and ninth in total games played (134).<ref>{{cite web|title=UCLA's Jaime Jaquez Jr. declares for NBA draft|date=April 6, 2023|publisher=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/ucla-jaime-jaquez-nba-draft-498c43c4a09c2e4665cbc959b198f45e|access-date=May 8, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Miami Heat (2023–2026) ===

==== 2023–24 ====
Jaquez was considered a borderline first-round prospect after his [[College basketball|college]] career and received an invitation to the [[2023 NBA draft#Invited attendees|green room]] for the [[2023 NBA draft]]. He was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] with the eighteenth overall pick, making him the only [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] player chosen in the first round. Jaquez became the first [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] senior to be selected in the first round since [[Darren Collison]] in [[2009 NBA draft|2009]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA's Jaime Jaquez Jr. drafted No. 18 by Miami Heat in 'surreal' moment|date=June 22, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-06-22/ucla-nba-draft-jaime-jaquez-amari-bailey-jaylen-clark|access-date=June 23, 2023}}</ref> He officially signed with the Heat on July 1.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Sanchez|first=Noel|url=https://www.si.com/college/ucla/mens-basketball/ucla-basketball-heat-officially-sign-ex-bruin-jaime-jaquez-jr-complicating-damian-lillard-trade-options-ns2002|title=UCLA Basketball: Heat Officially Sign Ex-Bruin Jaime Jaquez Jr., Complicating Damian Lillard Trade Options|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=July 4, 2023|accessdate=July 5, 2023}}</ref> Shortly afterward, he participated in the [[2023 NBA Summer League|2023 Summer League]] with the team but played only two games before a left [[Shoulder problems|shoulder injury]] sidelined him.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bartilotta |first=Joel |date=July 3, 2023 |title=California Classic Summer League: Jaquez Jr., Heat dispatch Lakers |url=https://www.nba.com/news/california-classic-summer-league-jaquez-jr-heat-dispatch-lakers |accessdate=July 5, 2023 |website=[[NBA]] |publisher= |via=}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Winderman |first=Ira |date=October 27, 2023 |title=Heat's Jaime Jaquez Jr. 'Not a regular rookie' |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2023/10/27/heat-drafted-jaime-jaquez-jr-as-a-ready-now-prospect-so-hes-ready-now/ |access-date=October 29, 2023 |work=[[Sun Sentinel]]}}</ref>

Jaquez began the [[2023–24 Miami Heat season|2023–24 regular season]] on a minutes restriction due to a [[groin]] injury sustained during the [[2023–24 Miami Heat season#Preseason|preseason]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Ira|last=Winderman|title=Heat's Jaime Jaquez Jr. 'Not a regular rookie'|date=October 29, 2023|newspaper=South Florida Sun-Sentinel|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2023/10/27/heat-drafted-jaime-jaquez-jr-as-a-ready-now-prospect-so-hes-ready-now/|access-date=October 29, 2023}}</ref> He made his [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) debut on October 25, 2023, in the Heat's season opener against the [[2023–24 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]], scoring his first basket on a layup with 26 seconds remaining in the first quarter, tying the score at 26–26.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Heat rookie Jaime Jaquez Jr. drives left for 1st NBA basket in Miami debut |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/jaime-jaquez-jr-1st-basket-heat-debut |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[NBA]]|type=video}}</ref> He finished the game with six points, having made all three of his field goal attempts, along with two rebounds, contributing to a 103–102 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Pistons at Miami Heat Box Score, October 25, 2023 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202310250MIA.html |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Three days later, on October 28, Jaquez made his first career start against the [[2023–24 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], filling in alongside [[Nikola Jović]] for absent veterans [[Jimmy Butler]] and [[Kevin Love]]. He recorded seven points and three rebounds in a 106–90 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Heat at Minnesota Timberwolves Box Score, October 28, 2023 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202310280MIN.html |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Ira|last=Winderman|title=Heat fail to measure up, fall 106-90 in Minnesota as Butler, Love sit|date=October 28, 2023|newspaper=South Florida Sun-Sentinel|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2023/10/28/heat-fail-to-measure-up-fall-106-90-in-minnesota-as-butler-love-sit/|access-date=October 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Heat's Jaime Jaquez: Starting against Wolves|date=October 28, 2023|work=CBS Sports|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-jaime-jaquez-starting-against-wolves/|access-date=October 29, 2023}}</ref> On November 30, he scored a then-career-high 24 points and grabbed 5 rebounds in a 142–132 win over the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indiana Pacers at Miami Heat Box Score, November 30, 2023 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202311300MIA.html |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2023 |title=Heat seeking repeat effort in 2nd of back-to-back vs. Pacers |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/heat-seeking-repeat-effort-2nd-back-to-back-vs-pacers--flm-2023-12-02/ |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Jaquez was named the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award|Rookie of the Month]] on December 4 in recognition of his performances in October and November, becoming the fifth Heat rookie to earn the award and marking the tenth time it has been awarded to a Heat player. He joined previous winners such as [[Caron Butler]] (four-time recipient), [[Kendrick Nunn]] (three-time recipient), [[Josh Richardson]], and [[Michael Beasley]].<ref>{{cite web |date=December 4, 2023 |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. Named KIA Eastern Conference Rookie Of The Month |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/jaime-jaquez-jr-named-kia-eastern-conference-rookie-of-the-month |access-date=December 4, 2023 |work=[[Miami Heat]]}}</ref> On December 25, Jaquez achieved season and then-career highs with 31 points and 10 rebounds in 39 minutes played during a 119–113 victory over the [[2023–24 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia 76ers at Miami Heat Box Score, December 25, 2023 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202312250MIA.html |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date=December 25, 2023 |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr., Heat slow Joel Embiid-less 76ers |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/jaime-jaquez-jr-heat-slow-joel-embiid-less-76ers--flm-2023-12-26/ |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> He earned a second consecutive Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month award for December, announced on January 4, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 4, 2024 |title=The Numbers Behind Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s December KIA NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month Selection |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/the-numbers-behind-jaime-jaquez-jr-s-december-kia-nba-eastern-conference-rookie-of-the-month-selection |access-date=January 4, 2024 |work=[[NBA]]}}</ref> Jaquez was selected to participate in the [[2024 NBA All-Star Game|2024 NBA All-Star Weekend]] Rising Stars Challenge and the Slam Dunk Contest, which were held on February 16 and 17, respectively. He concluded the season having started 20 games and played in 75 of the 82 regular-season games, the most on the 2023–24 Heat roster,<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023-24 Miami Heat Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIA/2024.html |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref> averaging 11.9 points and 3.8 rebounds while shooting 48.9 percent from the field.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jaime Jaquez Jr. 2023-24 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jaqueja01/gamelog/2024 |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=May 20, 2024 |title=JAQUEZ JR. NAMED TO NBA ALL-ROOKIE FIRST TEAM |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/jaquez-jr-named-to-nba-all-rookie-first-team |access-date=April 13, 2025 |website=[[NBA]]}}</ref> Jaquez was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]]<ref name=":0" /> and finished fourth in [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] voting.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023-24 NBA Awards Voting |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/awards_2024.html |access-date=November 24, 2025 |work=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

==== 2024–25 ====
In the final game of the [[2024–25 Miami Heat season|2024–25 regular season]] on April 13, 2025, Jaquez scored a career-high 41 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in a narrow 119–118 loss to the [[2024–25 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Wizards at Miami Heat Box Score, April 13, 2025 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202504130MIA.html |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}}</ref> The Heat had only nine players available for the game as several rotation players sat out ahead of the [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]]. Jaquez missed four of the previous nine games due to a [[Glossary of basketball terms#dnp-cd|coach's decision]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Anthony|last=Chiang|title=Takeaways: Heat closes tumultuous regular season with loss on career day for Jaime Jaquez Jr.|date=April 13, 2025|newspaper=Miami Herald|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article304086636.html|access-date=April 19, 2025}}</ref>

==== 2025–26 ====
Jaquez improved his minutes, points, rebounds, and assists per game in the [[2025–26 Miami Heat season|2025–26 season]], averaging 28.3 minutes and 15.4 points per game. He led the NBA in total bench points with 1,138, and was second in voting for the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]] award, behind winner [[Keldon Johnson]] of the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Anthony|last=Chiang|title=Jaime Jaquez Jr.’s standout season for Heat not enough to win Sixth Man of the Year award|date=April 22, 2025|website=Miami Herald|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article315493336.html|access-date=April 30, 2025}}</ref>

=== Milwaukee Bucks (2026–present) ===
On July 6, 2026, Jaquez alongside [[Tyler Herro]], [[Kasparas Jakučionis]], [[Kel'el Ware]], the rights to [[Nate Ament]] and four more future draft picks was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] and [[Bobby Portis]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Heat acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo in blockbuster deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/reports-heat-acquire-giannis-antetokounmpo-in-blockbuster-deal |access-date=July 6, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jaquez is of [[Mexicans|Mexican]] descent through his father, and of [[Norwegians|Norwegian]] descent through his mother.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Winderman |first1=Ira |date=November 30, 2023 |title=Heat's Jaime Jaquez Jr. laughing along with 'Juan Wick' nickname, as a proud Mexiwegian |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2023/11/30/heats-jaime-jaquez-jr-laughing-along-with-juan-wick-nickname-as-a-proud-mexiwegian/ |access-date=1 December 2023 |website=South Florida Sun-Sentinel}}</ref>

Jaquez is the oldest of three siblings.<ref name="usab" /> His younger sister, [[Gabriela Jaquez|Gabriela]], played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins women's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] and was named co-[[McDonald's All-American Game#Girls|MVP]] at the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Girls Game]]. She was drafted by the Chicago Sky in the 2026 WNBA draft.<ref name="Legacy" /> His younger brother, Marcos, plays [[college football]] as a [[Lineman (gridiron football)#Defensive line|defensive lineman]] for [[Ventura College]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gomez |first=Eric |date=October 14, 2024 |title=Inside the Jaquez Mexican American dynasty at UCLA and Miami |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41740597/jaquez-family-mexican-american-dynasty-ucla-miami |access-date=October 19, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>
